With Halloween just around the corner, it's time to get in touch with your spooky side. Whether you're planning a haunted house party, watching horror films under a blanket or heading out on a ghost hunt, there's no shortage of ways to get into the Halloween spirit.

If you're hoping to make this year's celebrations a little more hair-raising, the Erickhill EMF Meter, available for delivery for Halloween for Amazon Prime customers, could be just the ticket. The handheld gadget is designed to detect electromagnetic fields and is often used by paranormal enthusiasts hoping to track down signs of the supernatural.

Now reduced by 32% from £19.99 to £13.59, the device could be an intriguing addition to your Halloween kit if you're curious about the unexplained. Its compact design and colourful warning lights are also sure to get people talking.

The pocket-sized EMF meter is designed to measure electromagnetic fields ranging from 30Hz to 20,000Hz, including those produced by household appliances, Wi-Fi routers and power lines. It measures field intensity from 0 to more than 20 milligauss (mG), with a stated precision of ±5%.

One of its key features is a five-colour LED alert system, which indicates the strength of detected electromagnetic fields. The lights range from green to red, allowing users to see readings at a glance, even in darker environments.

Ghost hunters use EMF meters because some believe spirits can cause spikes in electromagnetic fields. However, there's no scientific evidence that ghosts produce EMF readings, which can also be triggered by everyday electrical devices, but it could make a fun addition to Halloween get togethers.

ERICKHILL EMF Meter

This EMF meter covers 30–20,000Hz, detecting electromagnetic fields from home appliances, WiFi routers, power lines, industrial machines and possibly uninvited astral visitors.

Hardcore hunters looking for extra inventory to add to their ghost hunting kit could also consider the GhostStop Spirit Box and EVP Recorder available for £77.99 at Amazon. The handheld ghost-hunting radio scans AM and FM frequencies to help users search for electronic voice phenomena (EVP).

For fright fans who want to have fun without the spectre of the undead haunting their houses, Ghost Letters is a fun but fearsome board game for up to 12 players. Available to buy for £29.45, the murder mystery game combines suspense and strategy for a thrilling time.

Shoppers who have already been brave enough to invest in the Erickhill EMF Meter have mostly been impressed, giving the device a 4.6 out of five-star rating on Amazon. One buyer said: "Great little meter. Checked all my electrical goods for high levels of electromagnetic fields, quite sensitive and easy to use with one button to press.

The continued: "For a bit of fun I took it to Basing House when there was a guided tour of all the ghostly goings-on. Sadly, didn't pick up any ghosts."

Another added: "Very good item, used recently and produced some interesting (and hard to explain) results when exploring an old disused fort. The results were consistent with those seen with other far more expensive equipment being used by others. Good entry-level kit."

A third said: "Works brilliantly as both a radiation detector and as a way to freak out friends during sleepovers. Pocket-sized, so I can casually whip it out like some kind of paranormal cowboy. Has one button that even I can manage that after a few drinks."

Not every shopper was quite as impressed, one person said: "The one button operation is simple and the LED lights are clear to read. However, the readings do not always seem consistent and can vary quite a bit when checking the same spot more than once."

Another said: "It's simple to use as it's basically a point-and-read device. The 5-level LED lights give a clear, immediate visual alert. Great for Beginners: If you're curious about ghost hunting, this is a perfect, low-cost tool to start with for fun."

EMF meters measure electromagnetic fields from household appliances, Wi-Fi routers and power cables, helping users identify areas with higher readings, but they cannot determine whether exposure is harmful. If you're planning a ghost hunt this Halloween, it could be a fun gadget to take along and add a little extra mystery to your spooky adventures.
